Grojec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Grójec, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Grójec began at the end of the 18th century; by 1921, 4,971 Jews made up nearly 59% of the town's population, and most were deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in February 1941 before being murdered at Treblinka a year later. The cemetery was established sometime after 1794 and expanded in 1847. In 1948, victims of a July 1943 massacre near Góra Kalwaria were exhumed and reburied here. Under German orders, some tombstones were used to pave a road during the war; under Communist rule, the site was mined for gravel and later used as a militia shooting range. A 1985 survey described it as a pasture and garbage dump with only 28 surviving tombstone fragments. A memorial funded by Mosze Kielmanzon of Haifa was erected in 2002, and the Nissenbaum Family Foundation cleaned up the site and built a gate and fence in 2003-2004; several dozen more tombstones were relocated here from private property in 2019.
